scenes.title: Leeds Environmental Tribology Workstation
scenes.institution: University Of Leeds — Advanced Coatings and Environmental Tribology Suite — Environmental Tribometer
scenes.reference_notes: The installed workstation has a front-opening rectangular metal chamber with a thick left-hinged door and circular viewport. Inside, a circular copper-ringed sample stage sits below a long contact arm with a vertical pin. A monitor/keyboard is immediately right, a control box is left and supported hoses, regulator hardware and a secured gas cylinder sit behind. Reconstruct only the observed tribometer workstation; do not merge adjacent coating/deposition equipment into one imagined room. Copper rings and service hardware are appearance only. Finite-stiffness normal loading and tangential motion are authored generic mechanisms. No calibrated friction coefficient, wear, heating, gas flow, vacuum or force metrology.

scenes.title: Copenhagen PICE Ice-Core Workroom
scenes.institution: University Of Copenhagen — Niels Bohr Institute PICE — Priorparken Ice Core Working Room
scenes.reference_notes: Two complementary official photos show a small cold working room with white insulated wall panels, a central rear freezer door, grey metal shelving, wood-topped blue-steel workbenches and a bandsaw between two benchtops. The saw sits on a lower metal stand with a guarded red guide and open upper wheel cover; storage bins and a small cart are below and beside work surfaces. Only Priorparken working room is selected. Do not mix in distinct ice storage aisles or other NBI extraction labs. Temperatures, ice phase change, cutting fracture, isotope chemistry and real handling/cutting protocols are not modeled. Room dimensions and original unpowered task fixtures remain estimates. The two viewpoints are reconciled as adjacent walls: the bandsaw/long worktops remain on the north wall and the closed freezer door is on the east end wall, with a shelf and cart outside its approach. This orientation and the 5 x 4.5 x 2.9 m room are estimates, not recovered camera calibration or a survey.

scenes.title: Lund MAX IV NanoMAX Imaging Endstation
scenes.institution: Lund University — MAX IV Laboratory — NanoMAX Imaging Endstation EH1
scenes.reference_notes: A real installed hutch photo shows a square multiport steel chamber at left connected to a long horizontal cylindrical flight tube running diagonally to a rear flange. Granite support blocks and an aluminium rail base support the entire assembly. A cantilevered actuator/slide projects into the right aisle; the rear wall/door is red, with high cable trays and a silver extraction duct. Lund University hosts MAX IV; retain that institutional attribution. EH1 and EH2 are endstations of the same NanoMAX laboratory and must not be counted separately. No X-rays, radiation, vacuum, fluorescence, ptychography, nanometre precision or microscope imaging is simulated.
